identity.title: The shadow of the Flying Saucer: A very low temperature for large dust grains

paper_type_evidence.quote: We thus observed the Flying Saucer at high angular resolution in CO J=2-1 with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) and the molecular clouds with the IRAM 30-m telescope.

evidence.quote: resolved the light scattered by (micron) dust grains in near-infrared with the NTT and the VLT and estimated a disk radius of $2.15''$, which is about 260 au for the adopted distance of 120 pc (cite: Loinard+etal_2008).

resolved the light scattered by (micron) dust grains in near-infrared with the NTT and the VLT and estimated a disk radius of $2.15''$, which is about 260 au for the adopted distance of 120 pc (cite: Loinard+etal_2008).

question.value: Can the temperature of large mm-emitting dust grains in the edge-on Flying Saucer disk be measured directly from its silhouette against background CO cloud emission?

evidence.quote: We attempt a direct determination of the temperature of large grains emitting at mm wavelengths.
under excellent weather (Cycle 2, 2013.1.00387.S)

analysis_steps.goal: Image ALMA CO cube and continuum

method.value: Calibrated data exported via UVFITS to GILDAS for imaging and analysis

evidence.quote: exported through UVFITS format to the GILDAS package for imaging and data analysis

method.value: Use J_nu(Tdust) ≈ Td/(Td−Tl(v)) Tc(v), with Tc from the 30-m spectrum, applied per pixel and channel

evidence.quote: Eq. [\[eq:tdust\]](#eq:tdust) can be applied for each pixel and velocity channel, allowing us to derive a datacube of dust temperatures.

assumptions.value: Extended cloud emission filtered out by the interferometer; disk in front of the cloud

evidence.quote: A smooth extended CO emission is filtered out by the interferometer whatever its opacity, leading to a null brightness.

validation.value: Consistency across velocities; effect of cloud structure tested with maximum filling-factor correction (Tc x1.9)

evidence.quote: This would increase $T_c(\mathrm{v})$ by a factor 1.9.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit dust disk model to the continuum

method.value: Vertically isothermal truncated power-law disk model fitted to the 242 GHz continuum, T exponent fixed at 0.4

evidence.quote: We analyzed the 242 GHz continuum with a simple disk model that is vertically isothermal, using truncated power laws for temperature and surface density and no dust settling
with 40 walkers and 5000 steps, retaining only the last 1000 steps for the error analysis
We ran an MCMC, using the “emcee” tool of (cite: Foreman-Mackey+etal_2013)

validation.value: Tapered-edge viscous profiles gave a poorer fit

evidence.quote: tapered edge viscous profiles yielded a poorer fit

findings_qualitative.value: Dust disk is very flat, indicating settling in outer parts

evidence.quote: However, the dust disk is very flat (flaring index -0.35), which is indicative of dust settling in the outer parts.

claims.hypothesis: Large mm dust grains can have their temperature measured directly via absorption of background CO
claims.experiment: ALMA CO 2-1 silhouette plus IRAM 30-m cloud brightness
claims.result: Dust temperature 5-8 K, T(r)=7 K (r/100 au)^-0.4
claims.finding: Dust is much colder than most model predictions

evidence.quote: We derive very low dust temperatures, 5 to 7 K at radii around 100 au, which is much lower than most model predictions.

claims.hypothesis: Disk is vertically thin and settled

evidence.quote: the scale height at 100 au is at least 8 au (best fit 13 au)

why_this_data.value: Edge-on disks maximize line-of-sight opacity and expected silhouette signal

evidence.quote: Edge-on disks are the best targets for this because their larger line-of-sight opacity maximizes the expected signal.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tapered-edge viscous profiles rejected for poorer fit

evidence.quote: tapered edge viscous profiles yielded a poorer fit

limitations_admitted.value: Missing short spacings and cloud structure on 7-10'' scales may bias temperatures; inner <40 au may be biased

evidence.quote: the inner regions ($< 40$ au) may be biased because of residual emission from the (warm) CO disk itself

limitations_admitted.value: Spectral index could not be constrained, degeneracy between temperature and surface density

evidence.quote: leave a strong degeneracy between the dust temperature and surface density, so no reliable value could be found

referee_caveats_inferred: Foreground/background geometry of the clouds is assumed
Tc at the disk position relies on a 10.7'' beam spectrum
Temperature exponent fixed rather than fitted
